clue.text: Explosive concoction produced by a descendant of Abraham

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
a brew is a mixture or concoction, as of drink

explanation.surface: Someone of Abraham's line mixes up a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for high explosive, a convention worth knowing; 'produced by' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrews, the Jewish people, trace their lineage to the patriarch Abraham in the Bible.

clue.text: You once wore stockings in the conservatory!

indicators.note: wore means one piece clothes the other, the stockings going round the old pronoun

parts.note: hose are stockings
thou is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation: you wore stockings in the greenhouse!
explanation.walkthrough: 'wore' is the container indicator: the stockings are worn around the archaic pronoun. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated glass building for growing plants is a greenhouse or conservatory.

clue.text: Show anger at the way many cut into the cheese

indicators.note: cut into means a piece is inserted inside another

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
St, street, is a way
L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for many

explanation.surface: Getting cross at how so many people slice the cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut into' signals insertion; L for many is the Roman fifty, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to react with indignation or irritation, like an animal raising its hackles.

clue.text: The variety of maple here is short-lived

indicators.note: variety of signals that the letters of the following words are mixed

explanation.surface: This kind of maple tree around here doesn't last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' suggests a botanical kind, but it rearranges MAPLE HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient that lasts only a day or so is fleeting.

clue.text: Take away and digest

explanation.surface: Remove something and then absorb it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to remove or extract, and as a noun it is a summary, much like a digest of a report.

clue.text: Fluctuate like the simoom and mistral respectively?

definitions.text: like the simoom and mistral respectively

explanation.surface: Comparing wavering opinions to two famous winds.
explanation.walkthrough: The simoom is a hot desert wind; the mistral is a cold wind in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to vacillate, and literally the two winds blow warm and chilly in turn.

clue.text: Creature making a row about midnight

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: An animal kicking up a fuss around twelve at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a tier; 'midnight' gives the middle letter of night.
explanation.definitionFit: A big striped cat is an animal, or creature.

clue.text: Fish and strong drink provided by one's mate

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink
a wife is one's spouse or mate

explanation.surface: A partner supplies food and liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American herring species is called by this name.

clue.text: A motto for cooking fruit

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A slogan for preparing fruit in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' is the anagram indicator; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the red salad item is a fruit, a berry of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Follow behind telephone engineers entering the pub?

indicators.note: entering means pieces go inside another

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to ring up is to telephone
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers come into the pub last, after phoning.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps; 'entering' signals the phoning, the article and the engineers all going into the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come last in a procession, trailing at the back.

clue.text: Up to that time nearly thirty comprehended the cipher

indicators.note: comprehended means took in or contained, so one piece sits inside the other
nearly means the word thirty is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Until then almost thirty people understood the secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims thirty to THIRT; 'comprehended' puts THE inside it, giving THITHERT, and the cipher O ends it. 'Cipher' looks like a code but means nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means until then or so far, referring to a past point in time.

clue.text: A hint of allure about the Orient

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: glam, short for glamour, is allure or glitz
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Exotic Eastern charm is just faintly suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places E (the East) inside GLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace or suggestion, as in a glimmer of hope, can be called this.

clue.text: 8's unusual name for a corded fabric

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: 8 refers to the answer to clue 8-down, a red salad fruit

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue yields an odd name for a ribbed cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the six letters of the 8-down answer into OTTOMA, then N for name finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a heavy ribbed silk or rayon cloth, as well as a footstool.

clue.text: Player engendering high tension around parts of Paris

indicators.note: around means the outer pieces enclose the rest

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for high, as on a pencil grade
T stands for tension in physics notation

indicators.note: parts of suggests the city's name is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A musician causes great stress in some districts of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' signals the French capital broken up and rearranged; 'around' has high and tension enclosing it. 'engendering' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays the harp is a musician, and a player is a performer on an instrument.

clue.text: Weapon in a hunter's grasp early in history

definitions.text: Weapon in a hunter's grasp early in history

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the run of words that follows, across a word break

parts.words: a hunter's grasp early in history

explanation.surface: Early humans hunted with a weapon held in the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'graSP EARly'; the whole clue also describes the primitive weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed shaft thrown or thrust by prehistoric hunters was among the earliest weapons.

clue.text: Like a secure telephone peacekeepers made use of?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, deploys peacekeeping forces
to have tapped a resource is to have made use of it

explanation.surface: A phone line used by the blue helmets that nobody eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'tapped' as bugged: a secure phone is one not bugged.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone that has not been bugged or wiretapped is safe from eavesdroppers.

clue.text: Bogus corporal's alias

parts.note: pseudo means fake or bogus
Corporal Nym is a comic soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V

explanation.surface: A fake soldier is going under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: Nym is a corporal in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name or assumed name is another name used in place of one's own.

clue.text: Unique new spectacles help us do so

definitions.text: new spectacles help us do so

explanation.surface: Getting new glasses helps eyesight beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer says we squint less with better glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal or matchless means one of a kind; with new glasses we need not peer so much.

clue.text: News broadcast round a single point

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
a single is one, the Roman numeral I
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A news item goes out about one particular matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' and 'point' look like geometry but give ammunition and a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A short news report on radio or television is called this.

clue.text: Native African extremists died in a gun scuffle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rest
a scuffle is a messy fight, so the letters are jumbled
extremists here are the first and last letters of the word that precedes it

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Radical locals died when a rifle fight broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' gives AN, the first and last letters of African; with A GUN, 'scuffle' makes UGANAN, and D goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a particular East African country is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Banish to unknown, isolated land, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and the result matches its pronunciation

parts.note: X is an unknown in algebra and an isle is a small isolated piece of land, together pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: Send someone off to a remote, uncharted island.
explanation.walkthrough: X (the algebraic unknown) plus 'isle' spoken together match the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel a person from their country is to banish them.

clue.text: Popular choice in list of services

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a voice in a matter is a say or choice

explanation.surface: A well-liked option on a menu of services.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill itemising goods or work done is a list of charges.

clue.text: Judge has stomach upset in primitive hut

parts.note: a wig stands for a judge, by the wig judges wear

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a maw is a stomach or gullet

explanation.surface: A judge suffers indigestion in a crude shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MAW into WAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed dwelling of bark or hides made by some Native American peoples is a hut.

clue.text: Envisage one taking drink in West

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so West gives Mae
gin is a strong drink

explanation.surface: Picture someone drinking out in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction but means the film star Mae West; 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to conceive or visualise it.

clue.text: Greek dialect making use of particles

explanation.surface: An ancient language of Greece involves charged atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the dialect of ancient Ionia, and in chemistry describes bonding through charged atoms called ions.

clue.text: Body of man found in saloon, possibly

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located within another

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, the 'possibly' marking an example
Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A corpse turns up in a bar, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar to go with the body, but it is a car (a sedan, in American terms).
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse, especially one used for dissection, is a dead body.

clue.text: Increase scope of a study on the Women's Institute

indicators.note: on in an across clue means one piece follows the other

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A research project on a women's organisation broadens its remit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-standing British women's organisation, famous for jam and village halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden or extend the reach of something is to make it wider.

clue.text: Get in lane, following diversion to the plant

indicators.note: a diversion turns traffic aside, here rearranging the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A driving instruction about merging, then a detour leading to a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' is a road sign as well as the anagram indicator; 'following' and 'to' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet briar, a wild rose, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Treatment to hand for fellow that's torn apart by dog

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: torn apart by means one piece is split open with another inserted

parts.note: that is abbreviates to i.e.
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Medical help for someone savaged by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment to hand' reads as first aid nearby but means care for the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic care of the fingernails and hands is a beauty treatment of this kind.

clue.text: The smouldering remains of love evident in divorced politicians

indicators.note: divorced means no longer married, so M (married) is removed

parts.note: members of parliament are politicians

explanation.surface: Lingering feelings show between politicians whose marriages ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorced' removes M, the abbreviation for married, from MEMBERS. The OCR text had a stray full stop after 'smouldering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing remnants of a fire, and figuratively the last traces of a passion, are called this.
